answer: An agent economy can cap how many agents one human principal may back: each principal stakes behind at most three agents, and any extra delegation burns its stake, like a river delta that can only split so many ways before the water runs dry. A sybil farmer cannot wander past the cap by minting more keys, because every fourth fake costs real burned capital, while honest principals sit at the nadir of cost with a single agent. Forging a thousand identities would need a thousand real backers, so cloning keys multiplies the price instead of the power.
